prompts.orient: 2. Read the memories on that element, which map where lists. Use Metaform's memory tool to store what you learn under the functional namespace of your assignment, so future agents working there can retrieve it: memory create_entities with node set to that address, each new entity with a short title and why.
prompts.counts: New = recorded by the last session here. Read them: metaform memory read_graph node=<address>
prompts.note_counts: The person's note: metaform memory note node=<address>

rule.why: The Join rule attaches all knowledge to the RE, so the next agent finds a memory where the goal it serves is borne, and memory cannot tell an RE from a PE for you.

rules.rule: Record each memory at the RE whose goal it serves, never at a PE that provides for it.

prompts.connect: – memory: read what agents learned at a node and record what you learn there, on its RE
prompts.recorded_unjoined: Recorded in the whole memory graph, at no node.
prompts.recorded_nothing: Nothing new to record: each memory and observation was held already.
prompts.stale: STALE: . Check it against the code before relying on this memory.
prompts.stale_counts: Stale = a memory whose cited file or lines changed since it was written; read it before relying on it: metaform memory read_graph node=<address>
